text:
mara: quick check — noticed a p95 TTFT bump (~12%) for gptx-13b-8k on hosted-prod around 18:10 UTC. Dashboard spike here: https://redwood/d/rt/ttft?panelId=7 :thinking:
cheng: saw that too, looks concentrated on the small-request tail (<=128 prompt tokens). not obvious on tok/s.
paul: @mara any recent batching or scheduling changes pushed yesterday? i remember a micro-optim to the continuous-batcher.
mara: yep merged #3345 yesterday evening — reduced max-batch-wait to 8ms. rolled to prod via canary at ~16:40.
cheng: hm that should reduce latency, not increase p95. might be interaction with prefix/KV warmup. opening a quick flamegraph capture on the affected nodes.
sami: i'll start a profiler snapshot on the gptx-13b pool. running: `./scripts/capture_perf.sh --pool gptx-13b-8k --dur 5m --label ttft-reg` 
olivia: heads-up: deploy-bot reports a canary switch at 16:39 -> canary-2 (sha: d12ac3). deploy-bot: "canary promotion completed" :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: canary promoted to prod at 16:42 (d12ac3).
paul: can we clarify the metric definition people are using for TTFT? is everyone measuring from request-received -> first-token-emitted at model-shard? or at the edge gateway?
mara: good call — current dashboard uses `ttft_ms{stage="serve"}` which is measured at the runtime worker (after rpc dispatch). but some traces capture gateway->worker so there is a mismatch. we should standardize.
cheng: proposal: define two metrics and labels — `ttft_worker_p95` (worker-side, excludes gateway queue) and `ttft_edge_p95` (end-to-end). queries: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ttft_worker_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))` for worker p95.
paul: +1. also add `ttft_sample_count` for significance and a `ttft_regression_tag` for alerts.
sami: profiler finished initial run — CPU isn't the hotspot, see big stall in KV cache warmup and sporadic memcpy spikes. uploading traces to S3: s3://redwood-perf/traces/1807802468-ttft.
mara: thanks. can someone run a controlled bench reproducer? i can provide a load script: `scripts/bench_ttft.py --model gptx-13b-8k --prompt-len 64 --qps 40 --duration 10m --collect-first-token`
cheng: running reproducer now on a dedicated cluster; will post p95 numbers and flamegraphs in this thread.
olivia: if it's cache warmup, we might mitigate by pre-warming prefixes for common routes. i've created a ticket in the backlog: PERF-411.
paul: quick code-review ping to @cheng for a small change to the batching heuristics — PR #3352. it's related to how we cap in-flight slots per shard; could affect ttft tail.
cheng: saw PR, will review later today. if anyone wants immediate rollback option, we can flip the canary config to previous behavior via `./deploy rollback --canary canary-1`.
mara: plan for now: 1) cheng runs bench + flamegraphs and posts results (eta 30m) 2) sami uploads full profiler output (done) 3) paul and cheng coordinate PR review and rollback option if bench shows regression 4) olivia files dashboard metric updates to show both edge/worker ttft and sample counts.
paul: sounds good. tagging @oncall in case we need emergency alert changes. :bell:
cheng: bench done — initial local run shows p95_worker up 9% vs baseline, flamegraph attached (short link): https://rwd.me/fg/180780. digging into memcpy hotspots now. will post final numbers in ~20m.
mara: thanks team. please drop small notes here as you have them — will consolidate into PERF-411 and we can decide on rollback by 19:30 UTC. :thumbsup:
